page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is an accelerated compute instance belonging to the Compute Optimized with GPU family. Built on KVM virtualization, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core using the x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem incorporates 40 MB of L3 cache, basic AVX support, and lacks modern vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 or AMX. Memory capacity stands at 60.0 GB, delivering 7.5 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU equipped with 16 GB of VRAM. Bundled local storage includes a 472 GB SSD, and baseline network throughput is rated at 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate clear architectural contrast between the legacy host CPU platform and the GPU accelerator. Host CPU performance sits low across general benchmarks, recording a bottom 10% stress-ng single-core score of 954.2, a weak multi-core score of 4765.11, and a mid-tier PassMark CPU score of 6724.43. Data compression, decompression, and database transaction benchmarks also trail modern standards, while Redis SET performance registers 5.6 million operations per second in the lower 25% bracket. Memory throughput aligns with older multi-channel DDR4 specifications, showing 37.47 GB/s uncached read bandwidth and 26.02 GB/s write bandwidth.

The instance delivers strong metrics in hardware-accelerated processing tasks. During large language model benchmarking, prompt processing on a small 135M model achieved top-tier performance at 9872.83 tokens per second. Running medium 7B parameter models, prompt evaluation reached 316.69 tokens per second and text generation sustained 42.77 tokens per second, both scoring in the top 10% tier. However, the 16 GB VRAM ceiling restricts larger models, preventing the execution of 70B parameter evaluations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge represents an accessible GPU compute node where accelerator offload dominates CPU demand. While general host computing efficiency is compromised by the older Xeon architecture, the combined 16 GB Pascal GPU and 472 GB local SSD make it well suited for small-to-medium deep learning inference, model testing, legacy CUDA-accelerated tasks, and static web serving offloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is an accelerated instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor, 60.0 GB of system memory, and a dedicated NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. It includes 472 GB of local SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. While the host processor exhibits modest throughput in general compute, database, and compression benchmarks, the P100 accelerator achieves top-tier results in small and medium LLM inference workloads, generating 42.77 tokens per second on 7B parameter models. The server represents an efficient deployment target for legacy CUDA workloads, small-model inference pipelines, and accelerated graphics or compute tasks that do not depend on modern AVX-512 extensions.
